description: How New Battery Capacity Helped California Avoid Another Blackout is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by California Independent System Operator; ICF International. New battery capacity in the form of battery energy storage (BES) units was a key difference-maker that contributed, along with demand response, to preventing blackouts during California’s extreme heatwave in September 2022. Coverage: California (2023). The toolkit gives California as the location, 2023 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
